answer:
Project Lead and Data Scientist are the two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems.

Under the default denominator D2 (proportion of the 194 respondents who answered the Q8 multi-select grid), the bootstrap (B=100,000, seed=20261021) gives Project Lead θ̂=51.03% [44.00%, 58.03%] and Data Scientist θ̂=48.97% [41.90%, 56.02%]. The Project-Lead vs Data-Scientist pairwise contrast is not statistically significant (Δ=+2.07 pp, p_two-sided=0.71502, Bonferroni p=1.0); however both roles significantly outrank Business Analyst, Developer, Solution Architect, Requirements Engineer, and Tester (all Bonferroni p≈0). Project Lead and Data Scientist are top-2 under all tested definitions D1 (n=276), D2 (n=194 valid), and D3 (excluding self-attributed respondents) — only D4 (self-attribution consistency) elevates Solution Architect to top-1 because of small n. None of the four definitions exactly reproduces the question-given point estimates 49.6% and 61.389%; the closest roles-specific match is a composite D3+D4 reading of Project Lead alone (48.77% and 62.50%, off by 0.83 pp and 1.11 pp respectively). The question-given CI half-widths of ~0.38 pp are too narrow for any bootstrap of the 276-row dataset (typical half-width ≈ 7 pp), indicating the question's point estimates were likely generated from a larger or differently-filtered sample; this discrepancy is a documented limitation, not an error in the ranking. -77 treated as missing; Q8_Others excluded from top-2 selection; Bonferroni across 21 pairs reported as a descriptive diagnostic only.

payload.hypothesis: Project Lead and Data Scientist are the two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems. Under the canonical 'valid respondents' denominator (D2, n=194), the bootstrap-derived 95% percentile intervals are Project Lead 51.03 % [44.00 %, 58.03 %] and Data Scientist 48.97 % [41.90 %, 56.02 %]; the Project-Lead-vs-Data-Scientist contrast is not statistically distinguishable (Δ = +2.07 pp, p_two-sided = 0.71502, Bonferroni p = 1.0). The question-stated 49.6 % and 61.389 % most plausibly refer to Project Lead under two complementary framings (D3 'association by other-role respondents' = 48.77 %, D4 'self-attribution consistency' = 62.50 %) while Data Scientist remains the runner-up by every definition except D4 (where Solution Architect's small subset pushes it to top-1).
payload.workflow: 1. Loaded data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv (276 x 202) and encoded Q8_ML_Addressing_<Role> as {quoted=1, not quoted=0, -77=NaN}. 2. Defined four candidate denominator definitions: D1=276 (all respondents), D2=194 (valid excluding -77), D3=D2 minus self-attributed respondents, D4=self-attribution consistency (P(Q8_<r>=quoted | D4_Role=r, Q8_<r>!=-77)). 3. Ran 100,000 bootstrap resamples (np.random.default_rng(20261021)) at the respondent level; reported 95% percentile CIs as primary and normal-approximation CIs as diagnostic; used Bonferroni over 21 pairwise contrasts. 4. Verified fix for the D3 mask bug (masks original self-rows by index, not by position). 5. Ranked roles under each definition, identified the closest-to-targets definition (D2, err=10.99 pp), and assembled the answer.
